chunks: Ali ibn Isma'il from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bukhtari from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding a man who buys a slave-girl from another man, and he says, 'I have not had intercourse with her.' He said, 'If he trusts him, there is no harm in him having intercourse with her.' And he said regarding a man who sells a slave-girl to another man, 'It is upon him to verify her chastity before selling her.'

key_terms.الاستبراء: Verification of chastity or checking for pregnancy

ai.seo_question: What are the rules regarding verification of chastity (istibra') when buying or selling a slave-girl in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies the reciprocal obligations of 'istibra'' in slave-girl transactions, establishing that the seller bears the primary duty to verify her status before sale, while the buyer is exempt if he trusts the seller's claim of no prior intercourse. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of 'istishab' (presumption of continuity) and the practical ease granted to buyers who rely on the seller's verification, distinguishing it from the stricter requirements often applied in other marital contexts.
